questions.question: What is academic vocabulary?
options: Formal words used across school subjects, like "analyse" and "demonstrate"
Words that only exist in dictionaries
Words with more than ten letters
questions.explanation: Academic vocabulary consists of formal words used in school contexts across subjects - more formal than everyday words but not as specialised as technical terms.

questions.question: Which is the more academic way of saying "The test showed that..."?
options: The test was like, you know...
questions.explanation: Academic alternatives to everyday words include demonstrated/revealed instead of showed, and believe/consider instead of think.

questions.question: In a task, what does the instruction word "compare" ask you to do?
options: Look at similarities and differences between things
Copy the text word for word
questions.explanation: Task words tell you what to do: "compare" means examining similarities and differences between two or more things.

questions.question: Which word would you use to organise a text by adding another supporting point?
questions.explanation: "Furthermore" adds another supporting point, while "however", "although" and "despite" introduce contrast.

questions.question: Why is it useful to learn academic vocabulary?
options: It helps you understand tasks and write better texts in all school subjects
It replaces the need for grammar
It is only needed in English class
questions.explanation: Academic words appear across subjects, in task instructions and in formal texts, so mastering them improves both understanding and writing everywhere.
